title: zia_url_categories refresh extremely slow on large URL lists — 5s API call → 18+ minute plan

blocks.heading: zia_url_categories refresh extremely slow on large URL lists — 5s API call → 18+ minute plan

blocks.code:
Terraform v1.9.8
on darwin_arm64
+ provider registry.terraform.io/zscaler/zia v4.7.18

blocks.item: `zia_url_categories`

blocks.code:
resource "zia_url_categories" "kosher_domain" {
  configured_name     = "kosher Domain"
  custom_category     = true
  super_category      = "USER_DEFINED"
  type                = "URL_CATEGORY"
  urls                = [/* 19,377 entries */]
  db_categorized_urls = [/* 33 entries */]
}

blocks.text: Full HCL is ~530 KB / 20,000+ lines because of the URL list. Available on request — encrypted via your GPG key if preferred.

Not yet attached. `TF_LOG=DEBUG` produces several hundred MB on this workspace and the relevant section is silent — the provider enters the resource read function and emits nothing for ~18 minutes. Happy to upload a trimmed Gist if a maintainer points at the slice they want (e.g. just the seconds around the `Refreshing state...` line for `kosher_domain`).
No panic. Provider read returns successfully — just very slowly.

Refresh time roughly proportional to API response time plus a small constant for unmarshal and diff. For a 5-second API call returning ~400 KB of JSON, refresh should complete in a few seconds, not minutes.

`terraform plan` refresh of a single `zia_url_categories` resource holding ~19,000 entries in `urls` takes 15–20 minutes per run. The same data via the underlying ZIA REST endpoint returns in ~5 seconds. The provider read implementation appears to be the bottleneck — likely O(n²) somewhere in URL list handling, state diff, or HCL marshalling.
Timing data — raw REST call to the same endpoint the provider hits during refresh:

blocks.code:
$ time curl -s "https://api.zsapi.net/zia/api/v1/urlCategories/CUSTOM_08" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o /tmp/kosher.json

real    0m5.259s
user    0m0.014s
sys     0m0.016s

$ wc -c /tmp/kosher.json
407552 /tmp/kosher.json     # ~400 KB

$ jq '.urls | length' /tmp/kosher.json
19377

blocks.text: Provider behavior on the same resource via `terraform plan`:

blocks.item: Init and provider load: ~10 seconds
Plan output emitted: ~18 minutes after `Running terraform plan...`
No errors, no warnings, no `still reading after Nm Ns` lines emitted past the 10-second mark
Net effect: a workspace with one large category cannot be planned within typical CI step timeouts

blocks.text: That is roughly a 200× overhead between the API response and the end of the provider read. Suggests one of:

blocks.item: O(n²) deduplication or normalization on the URL slice
O(n²) state-diff over the list
Per-URL allocation churn in HCL marshalling
Sequential validation per URL with no batching

blocks.text: `TF_LOG=DEBUG` shows the provider entering the read function and emitting nothing until plan output — i.e., the hot loop is inside the resource read, not in HTTP, auth, or rate limiting.

blocks.item: Create a `zia_url_categories` resource of `type = "URL_CATEGORY"`, `custom_category = true`, `super_category = "USER_DEFINED"` containing ~20,000 entries in `urls`. Real-world example: an organisation-wide kosher allowlist, phishing-allowlist, or large bypass list.
`terraform import zia_url_categories.<name> CUSTOM_NN`, or `terraform apply` to create.
Run `terraform plan` — the refresh phase hangs for 15–20 minutes per resource.

blocks.text: Smaller categories (≤200 URLs) refresh in milliseconds. Cost scales nonlinearly with `len(urls)`.

blocks.item: Tenant cloud: `zscalerthree`
Auth: OneAPI / Zidentity OAuth2 client credentials
State backend: S3 + DynamoDB lock (eu-west-1)
CI runner: Bitbucket Pipelines (also reproduces on local macOS Terraform)
Workspace contains ~80 resources total; only the one large `zia_url_categories` is slow — every other resource refreshes in under a second
Production tenants with kosher-domain, phishing-allowlist, or large bypass lists routinely hold tens of thousands of URLs in a single category — this is not a synthetic test

blocks.text: Workarounds currently in use, neither acceptable long-term:

blocks.item: Keep large lists UI-managed (loses Terraform as source of truth)
Run plans with `-refresh=false` for PRs that don't touch the category (loses drift detection)

blocks.text: Asks:

blocks.item: Profile the `resourceURLCategoriesRead` path on a 20K-URL category and identify the quadratic step.
If diff or normalization is the cause, switch to `schema.TypeSet` semantics or pre-sort to avoid n² compares.
Document a tested upper bound on `urls` length so users can size accordingly.

blocks.text: Happy to test a pre-release build against our tenant.
No prior open or closed issues on slow `zia_url_categories` refresh or scaling — search `is:issue url_categories slow OR performance OR refresh` returns 0 open results.

@(user) A performance fix for zia_url_categories on large URL lists shipped in v4.7.22 ([PR #576](https://github.com/zscaler/terraform-provider-zia/pull/576)). On our reproducer with a single custom category containing 20,000 URLs:

Fresh create: several minutes → ~35 seconds. Refresh: many minutes → ~20 seconds. Reordering URLs in HCL no longer produces a diff. Please upgrade to v4.7.22 and rerun your plan. The configuration that worked on v4.7.18 will continue to work on v4.7.22 without edits.
Closing on the shipped fix. Reopen with the v4.7.22 numbers if the refresh time is still unacceptable in your environment.
Zscaler DevRel

Thanks @(user)  — picked up v4.7.22 today and ran the same benchmark on the original repro tenant. Refresh time is dramatically improved as advertised, but the perf fix introduced a CustomizeDiff regression that blocks terraform plan on the same resource:
Setup:

blocks.item: Provider: zscaler/zia v4.7.22
Same single category as the original report: 19,377 entries in urls, 33 in db_categorized_urls, type = "URL_CATEGORY", custom_category = true, super_category = "USER_DEFINED"
terraform import succeeds; resource lands in state cleanly

blocks.text: Timing — much better:

blocks.item: Init + provider load: ~10s
Full workspace terraform plan (75 resources, refresh + diff): ~44s, vs ~18 min on v4.7.18 (~25× speedup ✅)

blocks.text: But the plan errors before output:
Error: SetNew only operates on computed keys - urls is not one
with zia_url_categories.kosher_domain, on url_categories.tf line 1, in resource "zia_url_categories" "kosher_domain": 1: resource "zia_url_categories" "kosher_domain" {

Looks like the URL-reordering normalization path in CustomizeDiff is calling d.SetNew("urls", …) on a non-Computed schema field. SetNew only works on computed keys. The reorder-no-diff behavior you tested in the repro is the code path triggering this.
Suggested fixes:

blocks.item: Mark urls as Computed: true (with Optional: true retained), or
Use d.SetNewComputed("urls") if you want to defer to apply-time, or
Replace SetNew with sorting the inputs in CustomizeDiff before the framework computes the diff (no SetNew needed if both sides are

blocks.text: pre-sorted).
Currently this blocks adoption: refresh is fast enough now, but no plan can be generated, so no apply, no merge. Happy to retest the moment a fix lands.
Reopening this issue (or filing a follow-up) since the fix as-shipped is not usable end-to-end.
Please upgrade to v4.7.23

NOTE: We appreciate the suggestions; however, we have specific reasons tied to our own API behavior on why we avoid leveraging certain aspects of the Terraform v2 SDK itself such as Computed or SetNewComputed.
Zscaler DevRel
Thank you very much for the quick update. Will test and update here 😃
@(user) Thank you for the incredibly fast fix. I tested v4.7.23 and looks like we're good. 17 URL cats, code over 20k lines and plan passed after 1m and 6 seconds.
You are the best!
